Bug lens:
1. isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||: the variable name says "admin OR owner" but the code requires BOTH simultaneously. A team admin who is not also owner is incorrectly denied.
2. Blacklist bypass: blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but guest input is compared as-is; mixed-case emails evade the blocklist.
3. sendAddGuestsEmails receives the unfiltered `guests` array, not `uniqueGuests`, so emails go to already-existing attendees and blacklisted addresses even though the DB write was correctly de-duped.
4. booking.userId can be null (guest bookings); using `|| 0` as a fallback passes id=0 to findFirstOrThrow, which either matches the wrong user or throws an unhandled Prisma error rather than a clean TRPCError.

Security lens: the blacklist bypass (finding 2+3) is relevant from a security angle too, but the primary label is bug since it is a logic/filter mismatch.

Performance lens: no N+1s or unbounded loads introduced — `attendeesListPromises` runs getTranslation per attendee but this is equivalent to existing patterns elsewhere in the codebase. No concrete material slowdown beyond pre-existing patterns.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` (logical AND) instead of `||` (logical OR), so the condition requires a user to be simultaneously a team admin AND a team owner to pass the authorization check. WHY: A user who is only a team admin (not also owner) will always fail the combined check and be incorrectly denied with FORBIDDEN, even though the intent (expressed in the variable name and the PR description) is to allow either role. HOW: Replace `&&` with `||` between the two awaited checks.
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of || so team admins are always denied

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with the original `guests` array from user input instead of the de-duplicated `uniqueGuests` array. WHY: This causes notification emails to be sent to guests who are already attendees of the booking and to email addresses that appear on the blacklist, even though neither group was added to the database. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Email notification is sent to already-existing attendees and blacklisted addresses because unfiltered guests array is used

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The blacklist comparison lowercases the environment-variable entries but compares them against the raw (potentially mixed-case) `guest` email string from user input. WHY: A caller who submits `BLACKLISTED@example.com` instead of `blacklisted@example.com` will bypass the blocklist check and have the address written to the database and emailed. HOW: Normalize `guest` to lowercase before the `includes` comparison.
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Blacklisted guest emails bypass the blocklist when submitted with mixed or upper case

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When `booking.userId` is null (which is valid for guest/anonymous bookings), the fallback `booking.userId || 0` passes `id: 0` to `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow`, which either matches an unintended user or throws an unhandled Prisma `NotFoundError` that is not caught and surfaces as a 500 instead of a clean TRPCError. WHY: The entire handler crashes for guest bookings rather than returning a proper error to the client. HOW: Guard against null userId explicitly before the query.
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Null booking.userId falls back to id=0, causing an unhandled Prisma error for guest bookings

I have enough evidence to synthesize. Let me form my final findings from what I've already read.

**Evidence collected:**

1. **`isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||` (line 46-48):**
   ```ts
   const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
     (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
     (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
   ```
   The intent is clearly "admin OR owner" (the variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`), but the logic requires BOTH to be true simultaneously. A team admin who is not also the owner will be incorrectly denied. This is a logic error.

2. **Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive for guest input (line 74-78):**
   ```ts
   const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(
     (guest) =>
       !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) &&
       !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)
   );
   ```
   The blacklist entries are lowercased (`.map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but `guest` emails from input are compared as-is. A caller sending `BLACKLISTED@domain.com` bypasses the blocklist. The schema validates email format but does not normalize case.

3. **`sendAddGuestsEmails` passes the original `guests` array (not `uniqueGuests`) (line 168):**
   ```ts
   await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);
   ```
   This means emails are sent to ALL originally-submitted guests, including those already attendees and those on the blacklist. Only the DB write is de-duped via `uniqueGuests`; the email send is not.

4. **`booking.userId` can be null → `findFirstOrThrow` with `id: 0` (line 58-61):**
   ```ts
   const organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({
     where: { id: booking.userId || 0 },
   ```
   When `booking.userId` is null (guest bookings have no userId), `0` is used, which either finds a random user with id=0 (unlikely but possible) or throws a Prisma error, crashing the entire handler with an unhandled exception rather than a clean TRPC error.

I have enough evidence. Let me now reason through all four pre-existing findings and check for any missed bugs.

**Summary of findings to evaluate:**

1. **`&&` vs `||` in `isTeamAdminOrOwner`** (line 46-48): The variable is named "AdminOrOwner" but uses `&&` — requires user to be BOTH admin AND owner. Since every owner is also an admin, this effectively means only owners get access, locking out admins who are not owners. This is a concrete logic bug.

2. **`sendAddGuestsEmails` called with original `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`** (line 168): The function sends emails to the raw user-supplied list, potentially emailing already-existing attendees or blacklisted emails. Concrete bug.

3. **Blacklist case-sensitivity** (line 77): The blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` (the input email) is compared as-is. A guest email `User@Example.com` would pass the blacklist check against `user@example.com`. Concrete bug.

4. **`booking.userId || 0` when userId is null** (line 60): When booking has no userId, passes `0` to `findFirstOrThrow`, which will throw a "not found" error rather than a meaningful error. This is a real but lower-severity issue (it does throw, just with a poor error message).

All four are anchored to changed lines in the diff. No new missed bugs found beyond these.
